assumptions: Compatibility claim: a RAID 5 usable capacity U in decimal GB (whole homogeneous parity array) is consumable as the decimal-gigabyte count N of the same stored volume for the byte converter.
Scope: decimal GB convention only; the array volume is the converter's stored object; filesystem-overhead and usable-vs-advertised exclusions are inherited unchanged from both bridged records.

gaps: Adapter-only record: admission projects the producer-view input port (parity_usable_capacity, GB, array context) and the consumer-view output port (gigabyte_count, GB, stored-object context); all vocabulary is admitted.
No runtime projection shipped in this research return; staging re-verifies the identity replay.

models.inverse_notes: N = U inverts exactly as U = N under the same guard. Check: N=400 gives U=400. Algebraic only.
limitations: Performs no conversion: both ports are decimal GB, and binary GiB volumes need the binary-side chain.
Asserts nothing about array fill state: a capacity volume is re-presented as a countable object, not claimed full or empty.

references.method: Independent producer arithmetic: n=5 disks of C=100 GB give U=(5-1)*100=400 GB; the adapter carries 400 to the gigabyte count.
